parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Group 2 carbonates decompose when heated.

Write an equation for the decomposition of the carbonate ion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe and explain how the thermal stability of the Group 2 carbonates changes with increasing atomic number.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Lead(II) carbonate, $\text{PbCO}_3$, and zinc carbonate, $\text{ZnCO}_3$, decompose on heating in a similar way to calcium carbonate, $\text{CaCO}_3$.

State relevant data from the Data Booklet and use it to predict the order of thermal stability of these three carbonates.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Dolomite contains the double carbonate of calcium and magnesium, $\text{CaMg(CO}_3)_2$, and some impurities. When $0.642\text{ g}$ of a sample of dolomite reacts with an excess of hydrochloric acid, $125.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is formed under room conditions.

Calculate the percentage of $\text{CaMg(CO}_3)_2$ in the sample of dolomite. Show all your working.

Assume that none of the impurities react with $\text{HCl}$.
